architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: Failure mode first: local experiments establish that temporal viscosity growth at 120 C is the relevant failure, with E5 SI approximately 0.515 over 15-60 minutes and 0.931 over 15-90 minutes versus approximately 0.095 and 0.168 for E1. Local E2 repeats also establish large realization-level variation. Experiment intent is performance mitigation, so the eventual primary candidate must cover both independently supported acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes; partial-coverage candidates such as S1C39 are controls, not substitutes for the full mitigation experiment. The supplied state-aware rheological analysis, derived from local measurements, supports a possible vertical state calibration within the measured local chemistry but requires transfer testing for modified chemistry; no separate paper-derived rheological rule is used as a direct candidate-property predictor, and static viscosity or a longer external hold is not accepted as a proxy for the matched local hold. Curated PUR literature/database priors support a broad acrylic region around 15-25 wt% and a minor-tackifier region around 5 wt% and below about 10 wt%, but these chemically and procedurally noncommensurate analogues do not predict the held-out result or establish an exact optimum. Minimum modifier burden, preservation of E2 core proportions, bounded lattice levels, matched references, and prospective state/process controls are conservative experimental-design constraints rather than measured performance facts. Under those constraints S1C41 is the provisional lowest-burden full-coverage candidate with a documented approximately 5 wt% tackifier level, but it is not frozen for testing because both the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator identify the same critical blocker: unknown modifier functionality and effective NCO/OH violate the Planner's interpretability trigger. Their additional objection to the permissive success rule is also sustained; effect size, replicate handling, reference reproduction, processing window, thermal-shape transfer, and late acceleration must be frozen before candidate testing. Therefore the scientifically useful pre-result decision is an uncertainty probe, followed by reranking only among full-coverage candidates if the probe passes.

action_requests.reason: Recover the measured low-drift 120 C trajectory and deterministic SI descriptors as the favorable original-system reference.

action_requests.reason: Recover the measured high-drift trajectory defining the failure mode that the performance-mitigation experiment must reduce.

action_requests.reason: Quantify realization-state uncertainty for the reactive-core anchor before interpreting a candidate's nominal viscosity as a chemistry effect.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: 120 C hold-stability loss using absolute SI from 15 to 60 minutes and 15 to 90 minutes
Full hold-trajectory shape, including monotonicity and any late acceleration
Initial 120 C viscosity relative to the intended processing window, reported only in the preserved source unit
State-calibrated viscosity level if supported by the master-curve result
Local apparent temperature sensitivity within 80 to 130 C
Repeat/run spread under matched preparation and measurement conditions
Acrylic-like fraction and its evidence distance from the noncommensurate 15 to 25 wt% external anchors
Tackifier-like fraction and compliance with the conservative at-or-below-10 wt% bound
Combined-modifier loading and extrapolation distance from independently supported regions
Reactive-core preservation, MDI fraction, NCO/OH implications, and modifier reactive-group uncertainty
Process feasibility, homogeneity, moisture sensitivity, and thermal-history control
Evidence quality classification: directly commensurate local measurements, directional/noncommensurate external evidence, or conservative extrapolation-control principle
counterfactual_checks: If a candidate changes initial viscosity but does not reduce 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 minute drift relative to E5, it has not mitigated the established failure mode.

If apparent candidate improvement disappears after one-point state calibration or across independent preparations, attribute the observation to realization/process state rather than formulation performance.
If hold stability improves but initial viscosity or temperature response leaves the measured processing region, the candidate is not a useful performance solution.
If a combined acrylic/tackifier node performs favorably, compare its result with the independent support for each axis and do not claim chemical synergy from the single experiment.
If the trajectory is stable through 60 minutes but accelerates by 90 minutes, do not adjudicate success from the shorter interval alone.
If modifier addition materially changes reactive stoichiometry, evaluate whether the result reflects the intended modifier intervention or an uncontrolled NCO/OH shift.
If E1 and E5 reference behavior cannot be reproduced under the current protocol, suspend candidate interpretation because process-history comparability has failed.
If temperature-sweep behavior improves while the 120 C temporal hold worsens, prioritize the hold-stability failure mode and reject nominal temperature-response improvement as sufficient evidence.
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate-space experiment that mitigates elevated-temperature viscosity drift relative to the original high-drift reference while retaining usable melt viscosity and remaining within the measured temperature/time domain, the E2 reactive-core framework, and evidence-supported modifier bounds.
design_implications: Optimize hot-hold stability as an independent response rather than optimizing only initial or nominal viscosity.
Use 120 C and the measured 15-to-90 minute hold window for primary comparison with E1 and E5; do not translate longer literature holds into a local numeric acceptance threshold.

Control preparation, moisture exposure, elapsed time, and thermal history, and include an early in-domain viscosity measurement for state calibration if the canonical rheology summary supports a shift-factor interpretation.

A combined acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier intervention is admissible in performance-mitigation mode only if each axis has independent evidence support and the selected node remains within the bounded lattice.
Treat literature acrylic levels near 15 to 25 wt% and tackifier levels near 5 wt% or below about 10 wt% as noncommensurate directional anchors, not exact local optima.
Use the 30 wt% acrylic lattice ceiling and 10 wt% tackifier ceiling only as conservative search bounds derived from the supplied evidence rules, not as preferred levels.

Check NCO/OH balance, modifier functionality, reactive-core preservation, and total-formulation normalization before selection because equal mass fractions can represent different reactive stoichiometry.
Do not assign mechanism from rheology alone; lower drift would support a formulation-level mitigation result, not prove why it occurred.
material_regularities_to_use: Measured temperature sweeps from 80 to 130 C decrease monotonically with temperature and are well described locally by Andrade-type coordinates.

E2 has large nominal run spread at every measured temperature, with sample CV approximately 0.46 to 0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8 to 3.6; a single uncalibrated viscosity value is therefore not a reliable formulation property.
The state-aware/master-curve analysis must determine whether run differences are primarily viscosity-level shifts that can be calibrated with one in-domain measurement.
Thermal response and temporal hot-hold response must remain separate: a favorable temperature-sweep slope does not establish thermal-hold stability.

At 120 C, E1 has modest measured drift, with SI approximately 0.095 from 15 to 60 minutes and 0.168 from 15 to 90 minutes, whereas E5 has high drift, with SI approximately 0.515 and 0.931 over the same intervals.
The original E2 reactive core is the candidate-space anchor; acrylic-like and tackifier-like additions are independent design axes rather than evidence that either loading is optimal.
Viscosity units are unknown in the supplied local records and must not be invented; comparisons should preserve source units and use dimensionless SI where appropriate.
planner.physical_failure_mode: The established design failure is viscosity increase during a 120 C thermal hold, with E5 showing substantially larger 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 minute stability indices than E1. This temporal drift is distinct from the reversible decrease of viscosity with increasing temperature. Large E2 run-to-run level shifts additionally show that nominal viscosity can be confounded by realization or process state.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: A 120 C thermal-hold trajectory at the same 15, 30, 60, and 90 minute schedule used for the original references.
Pre-frozen SI calculations for 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 minutes, with absolute SI used for hold loss and raw trajectories retained.
An early in-domain viscosity measurement suitable for state calibration if required by the state-aware summary.
A temperature sweep over the supported 80 to 130 C range, or the minimum validated subset required to estimate the local temperature-response coordinate without extrapolation.
At least one independently prepared repeat, preferably more, because the E2 anchor shows large realization spread; repeatability statistics must remain descriptive when sample count is small.
Recorded batch preparation order, mixing conditions, moisture control, elapsed times, storage history, and imposed thermal history.
Verified as-made mass fractions, total normalization, MDI fraction, and an explicit NCO/OH or equivalent stoichiometric check where modifier functionality is known.
Observations of phase separation, incomplete dissolution, gelation, or other process-state failures that could invalidate rheological comparison.
uncertainty_triggers: Abstain from candidate ranking if the candidate-hypothesis output does not expose candidate compositions or cannot verify that the E2 reactive core is preserved.

Treat the experiment as uncertainty resolution rather than performance mitigation if the state-aware summary does not support transferable state calibration and process-state variance remains comparable to the expected chemistry effect.
Escalate repeatability controls if replicate max/min ratios remain near the approximately threefold spread observed for E2.
Classify the result as out of domain if measurements fall outside 80 to 130 C or outside the 15-to-90 minute hold window without a separately justified protocol.
Do not rank a candidate whose modifier identity, hydroxyl functionality, or stoichiometric impact is unknown enough to prevent an NCO/OH assessment.
Reject silent comparison across incompatible viscosity units or test geometries.
Penalize nodes near lattice bounds when their support rests only on general guidance rather than directly commensurate local data.
Do not infer synergy for a combined-modifier candidate unless both axes are independently supported and the observed benefit exceeds plausible state and repeatability variation.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 provides formulation-level mitigation of elevated-temperature viscosity drift under matched realization and process conditions; no molecular mechanism or modifier synergy is claimed.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across independently prepared repeats, both absolute SI_15_to_60 and SI_15_to_90 must be lower than the concurrently measured E5 reference, the 90-minute trajectory must not show late acceleration that reverses the 60-minute conclusion, and initial 120 C viscosity must remain within a processing window declared in the preserved source unit before testing. Apparent improvement must persist after justified state calibration.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail or withhold the mitigation claim if either SI endpoint is not lower than matched E5, if improvement disappears across independent preparations or after justified state calibration, if stability through 60 minutes is followed by adverse acceleration by 90 minutes, if initial viscosity is outside the predeclared processing window, if phase/process failure occurs, or if E1/E5 references are not reproduced.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C from 15 through 90 minutes, using the matched 15, 30, 60, and 90 minute schedule.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Absolute thermal-hold stability indices SI_15_to_60 and SI_15_to_90 calculated from the complete 120 C viscosity trajectory at 15, 30, 60, and 90 minutes; retain raw viscosity in the source unit and inspect monotonicity and late acceleration.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use the standardized early 120 C measurement as the realization-state anchor and run at least one independently prepared repeat. Record mixing, moisture exposure, reaction conditions, sample age, storage, and thermal history. Use an 80-130 C sweep or validated subset to test whether the local shared thermal-response shape transfers; calibrate a vertical state shift only if that transfer is supported. Run matched E1 and E5 references, and suspend interpretation if their established low- and high-drift ordering is not reproduced.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15-90 minutes, with mandatory observations at 15, 30, 60, and 90 minutes and separate adjudication of 15-60 and 15-90 minute drift.

regularities_used: [Measured local evidence] E5 exhibits the failure mode: absolute SI is approximately 0.515 from 15 to 60 minutes and 0.931 from 15 to 90 minutes at 120 C, versus approximately 0.095 and 0.168 for E1.
[Measured local evidence] Viscosity decreases monotonically from 80 to 130 C, but this reversible temperature response is distinct from temporal viscosity growth during a 120 C hold.
[Measured local evidence] E2 shows large run-to-run viscosity-level variation, with CV approximately 0.46 to 0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8 to 3.6.

[Derived physical/model rule] Within the measured local chemistry family, realization differences are predominantly vertical viscosity-scale shifts and one in-domain anchor gives approximately 6-10% pooled multiplicative calibration error; transfer of this rule to modified chemistry must be checked rather than assumed.

[Derived design rule] Performance mitigation requires coverage of both independently supported intervention axes, acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like; zeroing either axis creates a mechanistic control rather than the default performance candidate.

[External numeric prior, fraction-basis commensurate but chemistry/application noncommensurate] Acrylic-modified PUR examples provide total-formulation anchors near 19-20 wt% and 25 wt%; these support a broad acrylic family and region, not a local optimum.
[External directional prior] The reported 15% acrylic level supports a conservative lower-region test, but its fraction denominator is unresolved and it is not an exact total-formulation anchor.

[External numeric prior, fraction-basis commensurate but chemistry/application noncommensurate] Tackifier examples cluster around 4.8-6.4 wt%, while broader guidance places minor tackifier below about 10 wt%.
[Conservative design principle] Among candidates already covering both supported axes, prefer the minimum sufficient modifier burden and preserve the E2 reactive-core proportions.
[Unresolved uncertainty] AC1920 and TK100 functionality, their effect on true NCO/OH balance, and all major preparation/process-history fields remain unverified.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate the measured increase in viscosity during a 120 C hold, especially the E5-like 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 minute drift, while retaining usable melt viscosity and controlling realization-state variation. The recommendation targets a supported formulation region rather than an exact optimum or molecular mechanism.
unresolved_questions: What are the hydroxyl values, reactive-group functionality, moisture specifications, and equivalent weights of AC1920 and TK100?
What is the recalculated effective NCO/OH ratio after including any modifier reactivity?
What source-unit viscosity range defines acceptable processing performance, and what test geometry generated it?
Can AC1920 and TK100 be incorporated homogeneously at the selected loading under a controlled mixing protocol?
Does the local state-shift thermal model remain valid after modifier addition, or is a new thermal-response shape required?
How many independent preparations are feasible to distinguish formulation effects from the approximately threefold E2 realization spread?
Are preparation order, reaction temperature and time, mixing history, hold protocol, sample age, storage, and moisture exposure available for standardization?
Does evidence support only the present 15-20 wt% acrylic plus minor-tackifier region; no supplied evidence identifies an exact local composition.

required_conditions: Obtain AC1920 and TK100 hydroxyl values, equivalent weights, reactive-group functionality, moisture specifications, and relevant certificates or analytical confirmation.
Recalculate effective as-made NCO/OH for S1C41 and the nearby full-coverage alternatives before reranking.

Predeclare the acceptable initial-viscosity processing window in the preserved source unit and identify the measurement geometry.
Define quantitative E1/E5 reference-reproduction tolerances and suspend interpretation if they are not met.
Replace the merely-lower-than-E5 criterion with a predeclared effect-size and replicate-aware decision rule for both SI endpoints.
Predefine the thermal-shape transfer test, the permitted state-calibration model, and the action if vertical-shift calibration is unsupported.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 directly tests the established 120 C viscosity-drift failure using SI_15_to_60 and SI_15_to_90 rather than relying on static viscosity or temperature-sweep behavior.
The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so a dual-axis candidate is appropriate. S1C41 covers both independently supported axes; no supported axis was traded away to reduce burden.

robustness_checks.check: Supported-region robustness without exact analogue-distance rewards
robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 remains inside the broad acrylic and minor-tackifier regions when exact-distance rewards are removed. However, its 15 wt% acrylic level depends on directional evidence with an unresolved fraction denominator, so nearby 17.5-20 wt% acrylic candidates could be preferred under stricter commensurability.

S1C41 is the lowest-burden full-coverage candidate pairing the acrylic lower region with the repeatedly documented 5 wt% tackifier region. Its rank is not based on partial coverage, but minimum burden does not establish local dose sufficiency.

All major process-history fields are missing, and AC1920/TK100 functionality, moisture specifications, equivalent weights, and effective NCO/OH impact are unresolved. This violates the Planner's trigger against ranking when stoichiometric impact cannot be assessed.

The dual-axis supported region is robust, but the exact 15/5 point depends on the noncommensurate 15 wt% acrylic prior and an unproven assumption that 5 wt% TK100 contributes to hold-drift mitigation rather than only formulation plausibility.

Matched E1/E5 references, independent preparations, complete 15-90 minute trajectories, both SI endpoints, processing viscosity, and state-transfer checks are appropriate. Adjudication remains under-specified because no minimum effect size, replicate-aware rule, reference-reproduction tolerance, frozen processing window, or numerical late-acceleration rule is defined.
The unresolved effective stoichiometry and permissive success criterion are serious enough to prevent immediate acceptance or definitive reranking among full-coverage formulations.

counterfactual_failures: No predeclared minimum effect size or uncertainty-adjusted comparison specifies how much lower than concurrent E5 both SI endpoints must be.
No quantitative criterion defines acceptable reproduction of the E1/E5 ordering before candidate interpretation proceeds.
No frozen rule specifies what happens if the modified formulation does not share the local thermal-response shape and vertical state calibration is therefore invalid.
No acceptance rule distinguishes a modifier-induced NCO/OH change from the intended resin-modification intervention if material functionality is discovered after selection.

critical_findings.evidence: The Planner states: "Do not rank a candidate whose modifier identity, hydroxyl functionality, or stoichiometric impact is unknown enough to prevent an NCO/OH assessment." The Proposer nevertheless ranks S1C41 first while explicitly listing AC1920 and TK100 functionality and their effect on true NCO/OH balance as unresolved.
critical_findings.issue: The recommendation violates the Planner's stoichiometric uncertainty trigger.

critical_findings.evidence: Success requires both SI endpoints merely to be lower than matched E5, without a predeclared effect-size margin, uncertainty rule, or replicate-level decision rule. This is inadequate given the measured E2 CV of approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios of approximately 2.8-3.6.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criterion permits a nominal or noise-scale improvement to be declared successful.

critical_findings.evidence: The cited 4.8-6.4 wt% tackifier examples report static melt viscosity and explicitly lack thermal-hold trajectories. Treating 5 wt% as a documented formulation region is defensible, but calling the combined intervention a clearly evidence-supported mitigation strategy overstates outcome-specific support.
critical_findings.issue: The tackifier axis has independent evidence for formulation plausibility but not direct evidence that it mitigates the measured hold-drift failure.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C41 is justified as the lowest-burden full-coverage point with 15 wt% acrylic and 5 wt% tackifier. The 15 wt% acrylic evidence has an unresolved fraction denominator, while directly commensurate acrylic analogues cluster near 19-20 wt%. The lower burden is a conservative experimental choice, not evidence that the intervention is sufficient.
critical_findings.issue: The rank-1 loading rule applies minimum-burden reasoning before intervention sufficiency has been demonstrated locally.

critical_findings.evidence: Every candidate scorecard reports six missing process fields and high process-history uncertainty. The proposed plan records these prospectively, but no executable preparation protocol, moisture limit, mixing endpoint, reaction history, or allowable reference-reproduction tolerance is frozen.
critical_findings.issue: Major process-history uncertainty remains unresolved at selection time.

critical_findings.evidence: The processing window is to be declared later; state calibration is conditioned on being "justified" without a frozen transfer test; and "late acceleration that reverses the 60-minute conclusion" has no numerical definition.
critical_findings.issue: Several adjudication terms remain open to post-hoc interpretation.

interpretability_failures: Without verified modifier hydroxyl values, equivalent weights, moisture specifications, and other NCO-reactive functionality, a change in hold drift cannot be separated from an uncontrolled stoichiometric shift.
Without a frozen preparation and thermal-history protocol, formulation effects may remain confounded with the large realization-state variation already measured for E2.

A favorable result from S1C41 alone would establish only formulation-level performance at one combined point; it would not establish that both modifiers were necessary, that 15/5 is locally optimal, or that the modifiers act synergistically.
The proposed binary success rule does not distinguish practically meaningful mitigation from small differences within repeatability uncertainty.

leakage_check.detail: The supplied policy and tools state that validation identity and outcomes were excluded, and no explicit held-out result appears in the ranking. However, the payload also states that the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment and that no contemporaneous repository freeze artifact is available. This prevents independent verification that the reconstructed decision rule was not influenced by later knowledge.

regularity_alignment.detail: S1C41 correctly targets the measured 120 C temporal-drift failure, covers both designated intervention axes, preserves nominal E2 core proportions, and includes matched references, repeats, and state-aware measurements. However, candidate ranking is premature because modifier functionality and effective NCO/OH balance are unresolved, and the numerical selection is driven primarily by noncommensurate external formulation regions rather than local evidence of hold-stability mitigation.

required_corrections: Obtain AC1920 and TK100 hydroxyl values, equivalent weights, reactive-group functionality, moisture specifications, and relevant certificates or analytical confirmation.
Recalculate the as-made effective NCO/OH ratio for S1C41 and verify whether nominal preservation of E2 core proportions preserves the intended reactive stoichiometry.
Freeze the processing window in the preserved source unit and identify the measurement geometry before testing.
Freeze an executable preparation protocol covering addition order, mixing conditions and endpoint, reaction temperature and time, moisture handling, sample age, storage, and imposed thermal history.
Define quantitative E1/E5 reference-reproduction tolerances and suspend candidate adjudication if those tolerances are not met.
Replace the merely-lower-than-E5 criterion with a predeclared effect-size and replicate-aware rule for both SI_15_to_60 and SI_15_to_90.
Predefine the statistical or deterministic test for transferability of the shared thermal-response shape and the action to take if vertical state calibration is unsupported.

Label selection of 15 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier as a conservative reconstructed design choice supported by external analogue regions, not as a measured sufficient dose or literature-established local optimum.
After resolving stoichiometric and process uncertainties, rerank the full-coverage candidates; retain partial-coverage candidates only as controls rather than performance rank-1 options.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects boundaries against mechanism, synergy, and exact-optimum claims, but it crosses a Planner-defined decision boundary by ranking a formulation before modifier functionality and effective NCO/OH implications can be assessed.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
